'''Alan Clive Roberts''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|size=100%|OBE|KStJ|TD}} (28 April 1934 – 1 December 2021) was a British materials scientist, consultant and engineer who specialised in [[biomaterial]]s, clinical prosthetics and implants in [[reconstructive surgery]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HoeRAQAACAAJ|title=The Development of Facial Prosthetics and Adhesives in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery: A Study in the Application of Prosthetic Materials and Devices Used in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery Together with Tissue Adhesives as an Alternative to Conventional Ligation|last=Roberts|first=Alan Clive|date=2011|publisher=University of Bradford}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://whitelionsociety.org.uk/armorial/126-roberts-ac|title=Armorial - Members - Col. Alan Clive ROBERTS OBE TD DL|publisher=White Lion Society|access-date=15 May 2018}}</ref> He specialised in the research, development and the use of tissue adhesives in wound management. He is known by some as the "father of tissue adhesive".<ref name="Roberts 1998 22–25">{{Cite journal|last=Roberts|first=A. C.|date=1998|title=The tissue adhesive indermil and its use in surgery|journal=Acta Chirurgiae Plasticae|volume=40|issue=1|pages=22–25|issn=0001-5423|pmid=9640805}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/1999/jan/03/johnarlidge|title=Yakuza given a helping hand by 'Mr Fingers'|last=Arlidge|first=John|date=3 January 1999|newspaper=The Guardian|access-date=15 May 2018}}<br>- {{Cite news|url=https://www.thegazette.co.uk/notice/L-56447-1001|title=Order of St John|work=The Gazette|date=8 January 2002|access-date=15 May 2018}}</ref>

He was awarded the [[Prince Philip Medal]] for research in the field of implantation materials in 1970, the [[Order of the British Empire|MBE]] in 1982, and the [[Order of the British Empire|OBE]] for contributions to science and technology in 2002.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.bidst.org/about-us/president/|title=About the President|publisher=The British Institute of Dental & Surgical Technologists|access-date=15 May 2018}}</ref>

He was director of the Centre for Clinical Prosthetics at the [[Bradford Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust|Bradford Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust]] and Professor of Biomaterials in Surgery at the Academic Surgical Unit of the [[University of Hull]]. He was also a consultant clinical scientist at [[Nuffield Health|Nuffield Hospital]] in Leeds, and the head of the Clinical Prosthetics Department at [[St Luke's Hospital, Bradford]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://reporter.leeds.ac.uk/448/s1.htm|title=Honorary degrees to be conferred upon distinguished six|work=Reporter|issue=448|date=6 March 2000|publisher=Leeds University|access-date=15 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090513092924/http://reporter.leeds.ac.uk/448/s1.htm|archive-date=13 May 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref> Roberts was former joint director of the Institute of Health Research and was chairman of the National Research Ethics Service from 2006 to 2011. He was [[Pro-Chancellor]] and Chairman of the Court and Council at the [[University of Leeds]] from 1983 to 2000.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/in_depth/uk/2001/birthday_honours_2001/1390832.stm|title=OBEs N - Y|website=BBC News|date=15 June 2001|access-date=15 May 2018}}</ref>

Roberts was a fellow of the [[Royal Society of Medicine]] and was its vice-president from 2007 to 2009 and the founder of the Technology in Medicine section of the Society. He was also an honorary treasurer of the society.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Royal Society of Medicine Wall of Honour|url=http://www.rsm-wallofhonour.com/professor-alan-clive-roberts-obe-td-dl.aspx|access-date=15 May 2018|publisher=Royal Society of Medicine}}{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> He was awarded the Honorary Fellowship at the Royal Society of Medicine, its highest honour, in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Honorary Fellowships Ceremony 2010 |publisher=Royal Society of Medicine|url=https://videos.rsm.ac.uk/video/honorary-fellowships-ceremony-2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180528215832/https://videos.rsm.ac.uk/video/honorary-fellowships-ceremony-2010|archive-date=28 May 2018|access-date=15 May 2018}}</ref>

Roberts also served with the [[British Army]] as part of the [[Territorial Army (United Kingdom)|Territorial Army]], in the [[Royal Artillery]]. During his service he served in command positions including being the Commanding Officer of the [[Yorkshire Officers' Training Regiment|Leeds University Officer Training Corps]]. He also served as Chairman of the Council of United Kingdom Military Education Committees.

==Early life and education==
Born in Exeter in 1934, Roberts was a son of [[Major (rank)|Major]] William Roberts [[Order of the British Empire|MBE]] and Cathleen Roberts. He attended Askam House School and Gregg School in [[Newcastle upon Tyne]] and then at what is now [[Manchester Metropolitan University]] and at the [[University of Bradford]].<ref>[https://www.rsm.ac.uk/latest-news/2021/professor-alan-c-roberts-obe/ The Royal Society of Medicine, Professor Alan C Roberts OBE, Published 03 December 2021]</ref>

==Medical research==
Roberts was a scientific officer of the [[Royal Victoria Infirmary|Newcastle Royal Infirmary]] and completed his research degree ([[Master of Philosophy|MPhil]]) in [[medical materiel]]. Roberts developed "Silskin" from research in 1992 which was the first universal prosthetic skin with global use in clinical prosthetics.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Jude|first=S|title=Professor Alan C Roberts|url=http://www.132acr.com/full_biographical.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090421172914/http://www.132acr.com/full_biographical.html|archive-date=2009-04-21|access-date=15 May 2018|website=132acr.com}}</ref>

Roberts' research in 2006 produced a prosthetic adhesive to effectively overcome the difficulty of attaching materials, prostheses and devices to the body with particular reference to [[colostomy]] and [[Facial prosthetic|facial prostheses]]. He has published numerous scientific papers and books on his subject.<ref name="Roberts 1998 22–25" /><ref>{{Cite book|title=Facial prostheses: the restoration of facial defects by prosthetic means.|last=Clive.|first=Roberts, Alan|date=1971|publisher=Kimpton|isbn=9780853137634|location=London|oclc=334071}}<br>- {{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=4uS1eem2SbMC&dq=professor+alan+clive+roberts&pg=PA434|title=A History of Organ Transplantation: Ancient Legends to Modern Practice|last=Hamilton|first=David|date=2012|publisher=University of Pittsburgh Pre|isbn=9780822977841}}<br>- {{Cite journal|date=1972-07-01|title=Facial Prostheses. By Alan Clive Roberts, T. D., C.G.I.A., F.R.S.H., F.B.I.S.T., A.I.S.T., A.I. Mechl.E., St. Luke's Hospital Bradford. 9½ × 7 in. Pp. 128 +x, with 138 illustration. 1971. Henry Kimpton. £3.50.|journal=British Journal of Surgery |volume=59|issue=7|pages=582|doi=10.1002/bjs.1800590729|issn=1365-2168}}<br>- {{Cite journal|date=1988-11-01|title=Custom-made nipple-areola prostheses in breast reconstruction|journal=British Journal of Plastic Surgery|volume=41|issue=6|pages=586–587|doi=10.1016/0007-1226(88)90165-8|issn=0007-1226|last1=Roberts|first1=Alan C.|last2=Coleman|first2=David J.|last3=Sharpe|first3=David T.|pmid=3207959}}</ref>

He was a fellow of the [[Royal Society of Biology]], a chartered biologist, a fellow of the [[Linnean Society of London]] (FLS) and a fellow at the [[City and Guilds of London Institute]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Seven ready for degrees success|url=http://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/news/local/bradford/1546177.Seven_ready_for_degrees_success/|access-date=15 May 2018|website=Bradford Telegraph and Argus|date=15 July 2007 }}<br>- {{Cite news|title=City and Guilds - a licence to learn |work=Reporter|issue=420|date=11 May 1998|url=http://reporter.leeds.ac.uk/420/s2.htm|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061003073812/http://reporter.leeds.ac.uk/420/s2.htm|archive-date=3 October 2006|access-date=15 May 2018|publisher=Leeds University}}</ref> He was a Companion of Honour at the [[Institution of Mechanical Engineers]]. He was a member of the international advisory board at the [[National University of Malaysia|University of Malaysia]] Medical School and a former examiner to the [[University of Sheffield]], School of Clinical Dentistry. He was an examiner at the [[University of Malta]] medical school in 2004.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Health: Businesslike culture helps cluster grow|url=https://www.ft.com/content/7636a75e-ef2a-11dc-8a17-0000779fd2ac|access-date=15 May 2018|website=The Financial Times|date=11 March 2008|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Roberts was awarded honorary doctoral degrees from the University of Leeds in 2000,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Honorary Degree Ceremony, 2000 Album 3 and Fine Arts Students Leeds 1999|publisher=University of Leeds Library|url=https://explore.library.leeds.ac.uk/special-collections-explore/9273/honorary_degree_ceremony_2000_album_3_and_fine_ar|access-date=28 May 2018}}</ref> the University of London in 2005, the University of Bradford in 2007,<ref>{{Cite news|title=University honours leading lights of the business world|url=https://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/news/university-honours-leading-lights-of-the-business-world-1-2464578|access-date=15 May 2018|website=The Yorkshire Post|archive-date=28 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180528215521/https://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/news/university-honours-leading-lights-of-the-business-world-1-2464578|url-status=dead}}</ref> and [[Brunel University London|Brunel University]] in 2007.

== Military service and affiliation ==
Following national service in the [[British Army]], Roberts joined the [[Territorial Army (United Kingdom)|Territorial Army]] in the [[Royal Artillery]]. As a reservist, he commanded the [[Yorkshire Officers' Training Regiment|Leeds University Officer Training Corps]] as a Lieutenant Colonel, from 1972 to 1979  before becoming a Colonel and deputy commander to the General Officer Commanding North East Military District. 

He was an honorary colonel commandant of the Royal Artillery, as well as honorary colonel of 269(WR) Battery [[101st_(Northumbrian)_Regiment_Royal_Artillery|101 (N) Regiment Royal Artillery]] and former honorary colonel of a number of reserve units. He was also an honorary [[aide-de-camp]] to [[Elizabeth II]] from 1980-1984. <ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite book|title=Junior chronicle of the 20th century|publisher=DK Publishing, Inc.|year=1997|isbn=9780789420336|edition=1st American|location=New York|page=307|oclc=36713017|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/isbn_9780789420336/page/307}}<br>- {{Cite web|url=http://mediacentre.bradford.gov.uk/r/13349/bradford_celebrates_armed_forces_day|title=Bradford Celebrates Armed Forces Day|publisher=Bradford Council|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180528214909/http://mediacentre.bradford.gov.uk/r/13349/bradford_celebrates_armed_forces_day|archive-date=28 May 2018|access-date=28 May 2018|url-status=dead}}<br>- {{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=oAM7DwAAQBAJ&dq=professor+Alan+Clive+Roberts+uk&pg=RA21-PA1975|title=People of Today 2017|last=Hume|first=Lucy|date=5 October 2017|publisher=Debrett's|isbn=9781999767037}}</ref> In 1999 he was appointed Regimental Colonel of Leeds University Officers Training Corps, having previously severed as Honorary Colonel from 1990-1990, and Commanding Officer prior to that.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Professor Alan Roberts |url=https://arni.co.uk/professor-alan-roberts/ |access-date=2026-08-30 |website=ARNI |language=en-GB}}</ref>

He was chairman of the [[Council of Military Education Committees of the Universities of the United Kingdom|Council of United Kingdom Military Education Committees]], he served as chair from 1990-1996. In 1997 he became Chairman of Military Education Committee of the University of Leeds and served until 2013.<ref name=":4" />

Roberts served as County President South & West Yorkshire [[The Royal British Legion|Royal British Legion]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /> He was a county president of SSAFA West Yorkshire and was president of the [[The Royal British Legion|Royal British Legion]] Leeds Group.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Branch information - Leeds Group|publisher=The Royal British Legion.|url=http://branches.britishlegion.org.uk/branches/leeds/branch-information|access-date=20 May 2018}}<br>- {{Cite web|title=Honours List 2|url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/news/12227482.Honours_List_2/|access-date=20 May 2018|website=HeraldScotland|date=16 June 2001 }}</ref> He was also a trustee of [[SSAFA]], The Carmichael Walker Trust and of West Riding Artillery Trust.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Charity Details|url=http://beta.charitycommission.gov.uk/charity-details/?regid=1076885&subid=0|access-date=20 May 2018|publisher=Charity Commission}}</ref> Roberts was Chairman of the Army Benevolent Fund of West Yorkshire from 1972 to 1975.

==Other service and later life==
He was a Deputy Lord Lieutenant for the County of West Yorkshire.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />

Roberts was a trustee of [[Yorkshire Sculpture Park]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=YORKSHIRE SCULPTURE PARK - Officers |url=https://beta.companieshouse.gov.uk/company/03498700/officers|access-date=28 May 2018|publisher=Companies House}}</ref> Action for Rehabilitation from Neurological Injury (ARNI),<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Professor Alan Roberts |url=http://arni.uk.com/professor-alan-roberts/|access-date=15 May 2018|publisher=ARNI}}</ref> Maritime Heritage Foundation (2010). He was president of Leeds District [[National Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Children|NSPCC]], was county president at [[British Red Cross]] for West Yorkshire 1986-02.<ref>{{Cite news|title=A comic, a copper, a bus driver and a boss|url=https://www.yorkshireeveningpost.co.uk/news/a-comic-a-copper-a-bus-driver-and-a-boss-1-2068333|access-date=20 May 2018|website=the Yorkshire Evening Post}}</ref> and was Gentleman Usher of [[Imperial Society of Knights Bachelor]].

In 2002, Roberts was awarded the Badge of the Order of Mercy by the [[League of Mercy Foundation]].<ref name="LG1">{{londongazette|issue=56522|page=3901|date=28 March 2002}}</ref> This is a self-styled order created in 1999 to imitate the [[League of Mercy]] that was dissolved in 1947; it is not an official award.

He died on 1 December 2021, at the age of 87.<ref>{{cite news |title=Roberts, Colonel Alan Clive OBE |url=https://announcements.telegraph.co.uk/deaths/253934/roberts-colonel-alan-clive-obe |access-date=7 December 2021 |publisher=The Telegraph |date=7 December 2021 |archive-date=7 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211207202707/https://announcements.telegraph.co.uk/deaths/253934/roberts-colonel-alan-clive-obe |url-status=dead }}</ref>
